A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same image-region concept bottleneck framework, renamed from GCBM to DCBM. Their main texts and appendices, including figures, tables and equations, are readable and support reliable matching.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification accuracies, concept-generation ablations, ImageNet-R evaluations, qualitative analyses and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds quantitative concept-localization results and concept-size filtering experiments.

M1.justification: v2 introduces optional filtering of concept proposals by minimum and maximum area before embedding and clustering (Section 3.1 and Algorithm 1). The core segmentation, clustering, concept projection and sparse linear classifier remain unchanged. Concept naming was already present in v1.

E1.justification: The classification datasets and domains are retained, including the appendix datasets. v2 adds localization in composite 2-by-2 images containing distractors on CUB and Places365, with an ImageNet-R illustration (Section 4.4.2). This introduces a distinct test scenario using existing datasets.

E2.justification: v2 removes ResNet-152 from the ImageNet-R comparison in Table 2. The DN-CBM results brought into that table already appeared in v1 Table 14, so they are not a newly evaluated baseline. The standard benchmark comparator set is retained.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a systematic localization protocol: combine each test image with three random distractors, apply Grad-CAM for its top five concepts, and average Gini, attribution-overlap and maximum-location scores over the CUB and Places365 test sets. It also adds area-threshold evaluation variants. Existing classification training budgets and backbone settings are retained.

E4.justification: v2 substantially extends validation of the central interpretability claim through quantitative Grid Pointing Game analysis (Section 4.4.2 and Table 4), beyond v1's illustrative grounding examples. Appendix E.2 also tests sensitivity to removing small or large proposals on CUB, ImageNet and ClimateTV. Most earlier ablations and transfer analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or comparable uncertainty estimates. Averaging the new localization metrics across test examples does not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds the first test-set localization outcomes and size-filtering accuracy results (Tables 4 and 18), while retained benchmark and OOD scores remain unchanged. It also revises CUB accuracy for GDINO Awa Low, CLIP ViT-L/14 and 10 images per class from 58.84 to 81.61 (v1 Table 18; v2 Table 16). The new localization table reports absolute scores of 0.6551/0.3445, whereas its prose quotes 0.7028/0.4988.

T1.justification: The normalized concept projection, linear predictor and cross-entropy plus L1 objective are mathematically unchanged. Expanded naming notation and descriptions of standard localization measures do not introduce new theoretical results, assumptions or proofs.

C1.justification: The core claims about dataset-specific visual concepts, adaptability, fine-grained classification and OOD transfer remain. v2 foregrounds the already claimed data efficiency and removes v1's explicit priority claims of first using image-level CBM concepts and first evaluating their generalization, narrowing the novelty assertions.

C2.justification: v2 explains weaker CUB localization through concepts shared across bird classes and explicitly limits applicability by segmentation-model suitability and CLIP expressiveness. It also states that interventions are absent and proposes automatic removal of spurious concepts. Earlier discussions of redundant concepts, visual-semantic mismatches and sparsity tradeoffs largely remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds pseudocode, explicit cosine-similarity naming, area-filter thresholds and clarification that CUB uses all available images for concept generation. Hardware, training budgets and runtime information already appeared in v1. The project repository link in v1's abstract is omitted, although v2 retains a public-code statement.

R1.justification: Sections 1–2 substantially reposition the contribution relative to existing visual CBMs around data efficiency, granularity and domain specificity. v2 adds modality-gap references, segmentation-based explanation work, and discussions of CBM locality, correlations and residual variants, while removing several earlier XAI references and the first-image-level-concepts positioning.

P1.justification: Beyond the title and model renaming, the abstract, introduction, related work and substantial portions of the methodological and evaluative narrative are rewritten. v2 places benchmark evaluation before concept investigation, creates a separate naming section and algorithm appendix, separates discussion from conclusion, and adds an impact statement.

P2.justification: v2 redraws Figure 1, extends Figure 2 with concept naming, adds localization and filtering displays, and reorganizes the qualitative figures. The original grounding illustration is removed; shower and botanical-garden examples move to the appendix. The unchanged NMI plots are split into separate figures, and appendix text and tables receive a substantial layout revision.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's illustrative grounding examples, v2 provides systematic localization measurements and a new size-sensitivity analysis, alongside clearer procedural documentation and more explicit positioning relative to prior visual CBMs. These provide a limited net improvement. Conflicting absolute scores between Table 4 and its prose weaken the new evidence, and omission of the direct project-code link reduces reproducibility guidance.
